THE WORLD-CONDITION PREDICATES (ODQ §934.50, design §18). WORLD_CONDITIONS is the frozen id -> predicate map; each predicate is (record, campaignState) => boolean, PURE, TOTAL and FALSE-ON-ABSENCE — an absent field yields false, never a throw, so a card simply does not offer the seal. The four sit in the map, return false until EM-E4 lands their state, and carry their source note AS DATA so a walker can tell a declared-absent predicate from a missing one. ⚠ THIS LEAF EXISTS BECAUSE THE CAP DEMANDED IT, MEASURED: operations.js already estimates ≈231-249 of 250 and ten predicates with their field reads are ~60 effective lines. It makes this packet's new logic-bearing leaves 2 of ≤2 — at the cap exactly. ≈60 effective of 250.

A5 proves the rename ops delegate to the existing cascade and define no rename logic of their own (HZ-JOINKEY). A7 pins design §15 in both directions and asserts set-institution-state('destroyed') and remove-institution are DISTINCT op types. A8 carries the ok/errors invariant and proves set-world-fact resolves no pool. Every negative carries its `// anchored:` marker on the line immediately above it. A CREATE row, not TEST — the validator refuses a non-CREATE row whose path does not exist (:709).

acceptanceCases.case: MAIN BEHAVIOUR AND GUARD-THE-GUARD, ASSERTED FIRST: OP_TYPES holds exactly the EIGHTEEN home types, set-equal both directions with a full offender list; EVERY row carries all ten declared fields of the declared type with guardsStated non-empty; Object.keys(OP_TYPES) is in compareCodepoint order; set-state is asserted ABSENT BY NAME (the chair's ruling 2; design §14 — system states are derived), so restoring it reds; and makeOp('set-field', { kind:'institution', id:'i1' }, {...}) returns an Op carrying the declared stage, consequence and four relations.

ABSENCE AND MALFORMED INPUT — NOTHING THROWS. An unknown type, a null target, { kind:'nonsense' }, a string op, undefined, and a payload with an undeclared key: makeOp returns null for each and validateOp returns { ok:false, errors:[...] } with the NAMED error, never a throw and never a partial op. validateOp(null) returns exactly errors: ['op is absent']. An omitted required payload field names that field; an enum value outside spec.values names that field. ⭐ AND THE WORLD HALF (§934.50): for a row whose requires.world names a predicate, a world in which that predicate is FALSE means the op IS NOT OFFERED, and a planted TRUE means it is — asserted inside this case, not as a new one. The four source:'EM-E4' predicates are asserted to return FALSE and to carry their source note, so a declared absence is never mistaken for a bug.

THE SEAT'S FLAG, AND THE STAGE PARTITION SET-EQUAL. set-power-holder's payload names a HOLDER and its declared writer is src/domain/rulingPower.js's transfer path; a source scan proves this module writes neither governingName nor government (matcher proved live on a planted string) — the name FOLLOWS the isGoverning flag, as rulingStructure.js's own comment requires ('it must always name the faction entry that carries isGoverning'). Then: OP_STAGES is exactly ['home','off-stage'] and OP_CONSEQUENCE_POLICIES exactly ['home','by-target-reality'], both frozen; every one of the eighteen rows is stage:'home' AND consequence:'home'; the two sets are SET-EQUAL so the fields can never drift; the off-stage members are declared but provably UNREACHED at this tip. Counterforce: consequenceFor is defined NOWHERE (EM-F1's) and rederive is called nowhere (EM-B2's).

RELATIONAL INTEGRITY, TOTAL AND CLOSED — the prevention guard. Every string in every requires / enables / relatedTo / conflictsWith array is a key of OP_TYPES, reported as a full offender list; conflictsWith is symmetric in both directions; requires and enables are exact inverses; relatedTo is symmetric. NO HOME ROW NAMES AN OFF-STAGE TYPE — the eighteen are closed over themselves at this tip, asserted by name, which is the arm EM-B1b re-runs over all twenty-five. ⭐ AND THE TWO KINDS ARE KEPT APART: every requires.world entry is a key of WORLD_CONDITIONS (full offender list) and every requires.registry entry is an OP_TYPES key — a world predicate appearing in the registry half, or an op type in the world half, reds. This is what stops the guards from judging a condition the card should have decided, and vice versa.

BOUNDARY — THE RENAME OPS DELEGATE AND RE-IMPLEMENT NOTHING. Each of the three rename-* types declares the right target kind, a single required name field, stage:'home', consequence:'home', and names the existing cascade as its declared writer. A source scan proves this module defines no rename logic of its own and re-implements no path listed in FACTION_RENAME_SURFACES — the join-key law honoured by delegation (HZ-JOINKEY) — with the matcher proved live on a planted string.

PURITY, DORMANCY AND THE IMPORT FENCE. makeOp and validateOp are proved pure: identical inputs give toEqual results, the input payload object is proved unmutated against a pre-call clone, and 100 calls change nothing observable. The import list is asserted EXACTLY and contains NONE OF src/kernel/prng.js, src/kernel/rngContext.js, any src/store/** path, any src/components/** path, and no force / muster / casualty / upkeep module. A source scan over src/** finds ZERO importers of this leaf, with guard-the-guard arms on both the walk and the matcher.

THE TWO VOCABULARIES ARE THE TREE'S, AND THE FIELD IS `category`. set-npc-status.payload.status is kind:'enum' with exactly the NpcStatus six (active, dead, exiled, missing, removed, retired) and set-institution-state.payload.state exactly the EntityStatus five (active, destroyed, impaired, removed, vacant) — each PARSED FROM ITS OWN TYPEDEF'S SOURCE FILE by the test so a typedef edit reds here; neither is kind:'free' (FINITE-SEMANTICS). `jailed` — named in design §15's prose and in the chair's fact (3) but absent from the typedef — is asserted ABSENT BY NAME, a recorded verdict rather than an oversight. set-field and add-faction spell `category`, never `archetype` or `type`, asserted by a source scan finding no such payload key, because archetype is a DERIVATION design §14 forbids editing. And set-institution-state('destroyed') and remove-institution are asserted DISTINCT op types. ⭐ AND THE TWO WRITE SHAPES (§934.47 add. 6): set-institution-state's pool is exactly {active, impaired, ruined, destroyed, vacant}; the four composer values are asserted to write the STATUS_* constants, and `ruined` is asserted to write the PULSE's shape (status:'ruined' with _worldPulseInactive:true) and NOT a composer constant. ⛔ EntityStatus is asserted UNWIDENED at its five, so the op offering `ruined` can never be read as having added it to the union.

THE ok/errors INVARIANT, AND set-world-fact AS A DECLARATION. For every case in a table of valid and invalid ops, result.ok === (result.errors.length === 0) — the two can never disagree, because ok is derived rather than set. errors is FROZEN and compareCodepoint-sorted, with a three-error case asserted in exact sorted order. set-world-fact validates `fact` membership against the seven world-fact keys and the PRESENCE of `value`, and is asserted NOT to resolve any pool and NOT to re-derive anything — proved by a source scan finding no rederive call and no pool import, so the design §14 engine stays EM-B2's.
